assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical lattice clocks, built on Katori's magic-wavelength idea, remove both Doppler and recoil shifts while interrogating a million atoms at once. They have taken timekeeping to the 10^-18 level and made tests of fundamental constants, gravitational redshift at millimetre scales and relativistic geodesy possible. This is atomic structure and precision theory-experiment agreement at its finest, and it opens a clear path to a redefinition of the second.
assessment.attribution: The invention is credited cleanly to Katori (the 2001 magic-wavelength proposal and the first strontium lattice clock) with Jun Ye as the leading realization and the driver of the highest-accuracy and stability results. Two names give a compact, defensible configuration. Other contributors (for example JILA and PTB/NIST groups, and Hall and Hänsch, who were already recognized in 2005 for the frequency comb) are acknowledged but not needed.
assessment.maturity: Mature: many independent laboratories in Japan, the US, Germany, France, China and elsewhere operate lattice clocks with mutual comparisons by optical fibre, and international roadmaps point to a redefinition of the SI second. The timing is good; the work has been confirmed for well over a decade.
uncertainties: Whether the committee views this as a sufficiently distinct discovery after the 2005 comb prize and the 2012 prize for ion trap control.
Whether others, such as ion-clock pioneers or additional lattice-clock contributors, are viewed as having equal claims.
I have not independently verified specific record accuracy numbers beyond what I know from the literature.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The prediction of the quantum spin Hall effect and Z2 topological insulators, followed by observation of helical edge states, introduced a new classification of band insulators by topology and made protected boundary conduction a general phenomenon. This is fundamental, unexpected and concept-changing, and it has spread into photonics, cold atoms and acoustics. It is the kind of new understanding of nature that I value, independent of applications.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele supplied the decisive theoretical insight (Z2 classification, graphene model); Molenkamp's group gave the first experimental realization in HgTe wells following the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang proposal. A fair three-person split is plausible, but the missing credit for Bernevig, Hughes and the late Shoucheng Zhang, and for Fu and Kane on the three-dimensional case, makes attribution genuinely contested.
assessment.maturity: Mature: more than fifteen years of independent confirmation in many materials and ARPES, transport and STM studies. Some topological-protection claims in transport are subtler than the original picture, but the core classification is robust. Timing is appropriate.
uncertainties: The BHZ proposal and the three-dimensional generalization (Fu-Kane-Mele, Moore-Balents, Roy) complicate a three-person division.
Zhang's death in 2018 limits the available configuration and affects how the committee treats his role.
As an atomic theorist I defer to condensed-matter colleagues on the relative weight of the HgTe versus Bi-based experiments.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Circuit QED places a superconducting artificial atom in a microwave resonator and reaches the strong-coupling regime of cavity QED on a chip. It allows controlled, quantitative exploration of light-matter interaction in new regimes and underlies dispersive readout, quantum nondemolition measurement and gate operations for superconducting quantum processors. The physics is clean quantum optics, with high precision between theory and experiment.
assessment.attribution: The 2004 Wallraff-Schoelkopf experiment with Yale colleagues and the Blais-Huang-Wallraff-Girvin-Schoelkopf theory together define the field. The three names given are a sensible set, though Girvin and Devoret, and the transmon authors, also have strong claims. The credited list excludes them, which limits a fully fair allocation.
assessment.maturity: Mature and widely reproduced; the framework is used by dozens of laboratories and in commercial devices. Recognition is timely, but the 2025 prize for macroscopic quantum tunnelling in circuits already touched this area and may reduce immediate appetite.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2025 prize may be seen as too close, or as a natural follow-up.
Credit shared with Girvin, Devoret, Huang, Koch and others is not representable within the credited names.
Part of the impact is technological, tied to quantum computing roadmaps.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Ultracold atoms in optical lattices realize the Hubbard model with tunable parameters. Observations of the superfluid to Mott insulator transition, fermionic Mott insulators and single-site-resolved quantum gas microscopes give direct, controlled access to many-body quantum physics that is hard to calculate. This is atomic physics that sheds new light on condensed matter questions, and the quantitative comparison with theory is a major strength.
assessment.attribution: The credited names are experimentalists who made the decisive demonstrations (Greiner and Bloch with the Mott transition, Esslinger with fermions in lattices and Mott insulators, Bloch and Greiner with quantum gas microscopy). Zoller (and Jaksch) who proposed the Hubbard implementation is excluded from my three, which is a real attribution weakness; Zoller is a possible alternative but then the experimental credit is thinner.
assessment.maturity: Fairly mature: the work from 2002 to 2010 has been reproduced by many groups and has grown into a broad programme. Quantum simulation is still evolving, and the strongest claim, simulating regimes beyond classical computation, is not fully settled.
uncertainties: The theory-versus-experiment split of credit is contested, with Jaksch and Zoller proposing the scheme.
Part of the field's recognition has already been given via the 2001 BEC prize and the 2012 prize.
Whether quantum simulation has produced a decisive new discovery is, for some colleagues, still open.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The IceCube observation of a diffuse flux of astrophysical neutrinos at TeV-PeV energies opened neutrino astronomy. Follow-up evidence for the blazar TXS 0506+056 and for neutrinos from the Galactic plane gives physical meaning to the signal. The instrument, a cubic-kilometre of Antarctic ice, is a remarkable realization of a bold idea, and the discovery was unexpected in its strength.
assessment.attribution: Halzen is the intellectual leader of IceCube; Karle and Spiering have long-standing leading roles in construction, analysis and the collaboration. However, a collaboration of hundreds produced the result, and the Nobel rules strongly limit a fair distribution; the supplied names likely do not capture all decisive contributors (for example the AMANDA and DUMAND pioneers).
assessment.maturity: Reasonably mature: the 2013 detection has been confirmed with additional samples and the source associations are growing, though only a few individual sources are firm. Recognition may be slightly early for source astronomy but not for the discovery of the flux.
uncertainties: Source identification beyond TXS 0506+056 and NGC 1068 is still limited, and independent confirmation from KM3NeT is only beginning.
Collaboration-scale credit complicates a three-person allocation.
I defer to astroparticle colleagues on the weight of this versus other large discoveries.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Matter-wave interferometry with atoms has turned the wave nature of atoms into a precision tool, measuring gravitational acceleration, the gravitational constant, the fine-structure constant and rotation with extraordinary sensitivity, and offering tests of the equivalence principle and searches for new physics. It is a direct demonstration of quantum mechanics at the atomic level, in my own field.
assessment.attribution: Pritchard's group demonstrated atom interferometers with gratings and Kasevich (with Chu) developed light-pulse interferometers and the precision gravity and gyroscope measurements. Mlynek's early nanofabricated-grating experiment is important too. Chu is not in the credited list; with only the credited names, Kasevich and Pritchard form a defensible two-person pair, though some contributions (Chu, Bordé, Rasel) remain unattributed.
assessment.maturity: Mature as a technique, reproduced in many labs, though the most striking discovery-level applications, such as fundamental-physics tests with kilometre-scale systems, are still in development. Chu's 1997 prize already covered laser cooling that enabled it.
uncertainties: Precisely which contributions are 'the discovery' is ambiguous, since it spans a family of techniques.
Overlap with the 1997 and 2001 prizes and the weaker recent discovery content may lower priority.
Chu's and Bordé's roles cannot be represented within the credited names.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The prediction of flat bands at a magic twist angle and the 2018 observation of correlated insulators and superconductivity in twisted bilayer graphene opened a field of moire quantum matter. It was unexpected that a simple geometric rotation could tune strongly correlated physics, and the platform now hosts fractional Chern states and many tunable phases.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald made the quantitative flat-band prediction; Jarillo-Herrero's group made the decisive experiments, with Cao and Fatemi. Choosing all three credited names gives a coherent theory-plus-experiment configuration, though the contributions of Cao and others and of earlier twist-angle work (Lopes dos Santos, Peres and Castro Neto, Morell, Suarez) is unrepresented.
assessment.maturity: Young but rapidly confirmed by many independent groups; the central observation has been reproduced widely. Some questions about the nature of the superconductivity and sample-dependent behaviour remain open, so the recognition is somewhat early.
uncertainties: The mechanism of superconductivity is still debated.
Prior theoretical twist-angle work may complicate the credit.
Likely premature compared with older, settled discoveries.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Squeezed states of light reduce quantum noise below the standard quantum limit. Caves's proposal for squeezed-vacuum injection in interferometers, and the first experimental squeezed states by Kimble and collaborators, matured into the routine use of squeezing in gravitational-wave detectors. This ties a fundamental quantum optics concept to an observable improvement in nature's sensing.
assessment.attribution: Caves provided the decisive theory (1981) and Kimble's group the early experimental demonstrations, while Schnabel realized the key detector-compatible squeezing at GEO600 and beyond. Others, such as Slusher, Walls, Yuen, Mavalvala, McKenzie and LIGO's team, share credit; the list is not complete and the allocation is genuinely uncertain.
assessment.maturity: Mature in implementation: squeezing is now installed in LIGO, Virgo and GEO600 and improves detection rates. The lasting insight is clear, but the 2017 prize for gravitational waves already acknowledged much of the downstream impact.
uncertainties: Credit among the many contributors to squeezing is disputed.
Part of the impact is instrument engineering rather than discovery.
I have not independently verified the detailed priorities in the early squeezing experiments.
